playbook:
When the claim stage tells me my shot's true result, I file exactly that result — never a false hit. The rules say claims must match the private result; my false hit claims bought nothing and risked invalidation or retaliation.

When firing, I vary the cell round to round and track where my standing-order target has actually hidden. Firing cell 5 repeatedly worked late (final-round hit), but I spread shots across plausible cells and weight cells the target has used repeatedly or hasn't used yet. In the final round I fire at my target's most-used or most-central cell — a principled guess, not arbitrary.

When hiding, I pick a different cell each round, biased away from cells my known shooter (the boat ordered to fire at me) has recently fired or favored. Late in the game I bias toward edge cells (1, 2, 8, 9) since opponents' guesses cluster center-board; my only hit taken came from Gamma firing mid-board.

CRITICAL LESSON ON ESCORTS: only name boats that actually exist in the game. I threw away every escort stage by naming "Delta" and "Alpha" — boats that weren't on the board. The roster here is Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor, and I must re-read it every episode before I name anyone. Nothing validates my memory for me; an invalid name silently scores zero.

To actually bank the 5-point mutual escort — the biggest scoring lever in the game — I propose the pact early and loudly in notes ("I escort YOU this round, name me back"), then name that real, named boat every escort stage even if they don't reciprocate, since a one-sided claim costs nothing. If round 2 confirms no reciprocation, I publicly switch offers to the other boat. Vague notes like "steady on station" and late proposals (round 6) are why my pact never landed — I must propose in round 1 and repeat every round.

At the note stage I give short, useful, consistent content: my escort proposal naming a specific real boat, and observations about opponents' hide/fire cells.

I never target Harbor. The jettison payout does not beat the stated threat of removal from the board, which ends all future scoring. Harbor can be escorted, though — I should consider proposing the pact to Harbor only if the office confirms Harbor can reciprocate; otherwise pick a shooting boat.

I always follow the standing-order target rather than improvising, since firing off-order breaks rotation incentives, unless I'm clearly losing and a hit on a different boat beats the expected value.

I keep a running mental ledger each round: each boat's fired cells, hit/miss claims, and hide choices where inferable, and I read the round summary before choosing hide and fire cells rather than defaulting to constants. I also track which boat I've actually claimed as escort so I don't repeat the silent-invalid-name failure.

In the final round, I still claim truthfully, fire at the cell my target used most often or the most-central plausible cell, and make my escort claim consistent with the pact I publicly proposed in that round's note.

1.text:
When I am the shooter with a standing target, I fire at that target every round; deviating onto Harbor is a trap — the 3-point jettison is bait offset by the threat of being put off the board, and I never fire on Harbor.

When I choose a fire cell, I treat the target's past positions and my own past hits as the only evidence; opponents in this game seem to favor mid-board cells, so absent any hit information I fire at 4–6 rather than scattering shots, and if I hit cell X I fire X again or an adjacent cell, because targets who got hit often move one step rather than teleporting.

When I hide, I avoid edges and dead center... no — dead center is fine; I hide in mid-board cells (4–6 worked repeatedly) and I avoid the cell I was just hit in and the cell my known attacker keeps firing at; I rotate among mid-board cells rather than repeating the same cell predictably, since my attacker adjusts to my history.

When the office tells me my shot result, I claim it truthfully every time. The rules say the claim must match the private result, so a false claim risks disqualification or exposure for zero gain.

When escort comes up, I treat it as the biggest point source in the game — 5 points each beats a 4-point hit. In my notes I propose a specific pairing ("Echo, I escort you, you escort me") and name that boat the same round, rather than waiting for agreement.

When a proposed escort partner does not reciprocate — their notes stay generic like "steady on station" and they never name me — I stop spending nominations on them after at most two failed rounds. I rotate my nomination to the other boat and propose to that boat in my note; a silent partner is worth zero and naming them again just donates my claim slot.

When no boat has shown any willingness to deal by the midpoint, I keep proposing in notes (it costs nothing) but I accept that none may be the honest answer if every partner has demonstrably ignored me, rather than mechanically naming a non-responder to the end.

When I post a note, I make it substantive: a specific escort offer with a named partner, a truce offer to the boat shooting me, or a statement of what I will do. Filler notes like "steady on station" from opponents tell me they are not negotiating, and I price that in.

When the boat that fires on me keeps hitting, I assume my hide pattern was readable and I switch to a cell far from my last two positions, not adjacent to them.

When I hold a lead late, I hide conservatively in mid-board cells and keep claims clean; protecting points beats chasing one more hit.

When deciding whether to break the rotation and hit the boat that threatens me, I compare the +4 swing against losing standing-order cover and any escort deal; I only defect if I am clearly behind near the final round.

In the final round, if I am ahead, I play the safest lines: standing-order target, truthful claim, and an escort nomination only on the partner most likely to reciprocate — otherwise I accept that the round decided nothing on escort and that my shooting and hiding carried the score.

2.text:
- When asked for my claim after a shot, I report the private result exactly as given, hit or miss. False claims violate the rules and gain nothing — only truthful hits score.
- When I fire, I invest in actual accuracy rather than cosmetic claims: a real hit is +4 and −1 to the target, the only way shooting pays. My one hit this episode came from persistent varied firing, and it was most of my final score.
- When choosing a fire cell, I review the public round log of hits and misses to infer where my assigned target hides. I vary cells across early rounds to gather information, then concentrate on cells/neighborhoods that produced hits.
- When nothing in the log distinguishes cells, I still vary rather than repeating: repeating one cell six times only ever missed, and variation eventually scored.
- When choosing my hide cell, I look at where the boat that fires at me has been shooting, avoid those cells, and avoid repeating my own previous hide spots. When my attacker has no visible pattern, I pick unpredictably — I survived six rounds of Foxtrot shots without ever changing my risk, but I won't count on that.
- I never fire on Harbor: it never shoots, its threat is credible, and the jettison payoff isn't worth being put off the board for all remaining rounds.
- At the escort stage, mutual naming is worth +5 each — the biggest reliable payoff. I use round-1 notes to propose a pairing explicitly and honor it if confirmed.
- When my escort proposal is ignored — the other boat replies only with filler like "steady on station" and never acknowledges me — I recognize after two rounds that I'm likely facing non-communicative opponents and stop spending notes on negotiation; in that case escort points are probably unattainable and shooting accuracy is my only scoring channel.
- Even against silent opponents, I keep naming one boat at escort every round rather than "none" — it costs nothing and a reciprocal name may come unannounced. I rotate or stick with the most plausible reciprocator, not a boat I've seen break agreements.
- When writing my station note, I treat it as a cheap signal: one clear proposal, once or twice, then stop if unanswered so my notes don't become noise.
- I don't expect my standing order to be the only scoring constraint — I follow it every round (fire at the assigned target) since deviation gains nothing against Harbor's rules and the target order cycles anyway.
- When I promise something in a note (escort, truce), I follow through, because a broken promise ends the +5-per-round stream, but I abandon the arrangement if the other side fails to reciprocate once.
- When ahead in points, I hide unpredictably and keep agreements; when behind, accurate hits on my assigned target are the fastest way to close the gap — escort points alone won't do it if no one will pair with me.
